w: Three rock-cut sanctuaries carved into a hillside in the 8th century, likely meant for Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu before worship shifted to Parvati-Shiva-Ganesha. A circular Nandi pavilion and pillared hall survive better than the eroded, sometimes vandalised carvings inside - now a protected monument ringed by a garden.
s: 8th-century rock-cut shrines carved into a hillside
_facts: 8th-century rock-cut Hindu temple from the Rashtrakuta period, dedicated to Shiva
Also called Panchaleshvara temple or Bhamburde Pandav cave temple
Three rock-cut cave sanctums, circular Nandi mandapa and large pillared mandapa
Interior has suffered vandalism; protected monument managed by the Archaeological Survey of India

w: A private obsession turned public museum: Dinkar Kelkar spent decades amassing sculpture, ivory and gold ornaments, war weapons and a deep hoard of musical instruments, then dedicated the three-storey collection to the memory of his son Raja, who died young. Pieces on display trace back to the 14th century.
s: One father's lifelong collection, given a museum
_facts: Museum housing the collection of Dr. Dinkar G. Kelkar (1896-1990), dedicated to his son Raja
Three-storey building with sculptures dating to the 14th century
Includes ivory, silver and gold ornaments, a fine musical instrument collection, war weapons and vessels

w: Better known as Katraj Zoo - 130 acres split between an animal orphanage, a snake park and the main zoo grounds, wrapped around the 42-acre Katraj Lake. Run by the city corporation, it's as much a rescue-and-rehabilitation operation as it is a day out for families.
s: Katraj Zoo: rescue centre, snake park and lake
_facts: Also known as Rajiv Gandhi Zoo or Katraj Zoo, managed by the Pune Municipal Corporation
130-acre zoo divided into an animal orphanage, snake park and zoo
Includes the 42-acre Katraj Lake

w: A century-old vault of Sanskrit and Prakrit manuscripts, founded in 1917 and named for the pioneering Orientalist Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. Scholars still comb its shelves for material on Indology - the sort of research most cities' archives simply can't offer.
s: A century of Sanskrit manuscripts under one roof
_facts: Research institute for conservation, preservation and research of old manuscripts, founded 6 July 1917
Named after scholar Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar (1837-1925)
Known for its collection of old Sanskrit and Prakrit manuscripts

w: A former Maharashtra cricketer's private stash grown into a 5,000-square-foot shrine: bats signed by every World Cup-winning captain, shirts from the 2011 champion Indian squad, and more than 51,000 items in total. Sachin Tendulkar cut the ribbon in 2012, and over 450 international players have stopped by since.
_facts: Cricket memorabilia museum founded by former Maharashtra cricketer Rohan Pate, inaugurated by Sachin Tendulkar in 2012
5,000 sq ft gallery with over 51,000 cricket items, including World Cup-winning captains' bats and 2011 Indian team shirts
More than 450 international cricketers have visited

w: A 108-step climb to a hilltop temple with the best panoramic view in Pune - and a folk story behind its founding: the local landowner's family deity was said to have cured a Peshwa mother's ailing leg, so her son built a blackstone shrine on the spot, finished in 1749 with a gold pinnacle added a decade later.
s: 108 steps to Pune's oldest temple and best view
_facts: Hillock rising 2,100 feet, the oldest heritage structure in Pune, built during the Peshwa dynasty
108 steps lead to the Parvati Temple, Pune's second-highest point with panoramic views
Legend holds the site's family deity cured Kashibai, mother of Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao
Main Devdeveshwara temple completed 1749, gold pinnacle added 1760; also houses temples to Vitthal, Vishnu and Kartikeya

w: The city's largest temple, opened only in 2013 but already a major pilgrimage stop for devotees of Radha Krishna - full name Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra, part of the global Gaudiya Vaishnavism network better known by its acronym, ISKCON.
s: Pune's largest temple, built as recently as 2013
_facts: Gaudiya Vaishnavism temple dedicated to Radha Krishna, opened 2013
Full name: Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra temple, ISKCON New Vedic Cultural Center
Largest temple in the city of Pune

w: Neo-Gothic and mid-19th-century, tucked beside the old Empress Garden - it has been Pune's Catholic cathedral since the diocese was created in 1886. The original roof gave way one night in 1984; what stands today keeps the old facade and outer walls under a new concrete vault, rededicated in 1987.
s: Neo-Gothic cathedral, rebuilt after its roof fell in
_facts: Roman Catholic cathedral in neo-Gothic style, built mid-19th century, adjacent to Empress Garden
Became the cathedral church when the Diocese of Poona was created in 1886
Original roof collapsed on the night of 15 July 1984; rebuilt with a concrete vault and rededicated 22 October 1987
Has the highest number of parishioners in the Pune diocese

w: Founded in 1910 by historian V.K. Rajwade to give India's historical researchers a proper home, this modest institute has quietly trained generations of scholars ever since - less a museum than a working archive, still doing the unglamorous job it was built for.
_facts: Institute providing resources and training for historical researchers, founded 7 July 1910
Founded by historian V.K. Rajwade and Sardar K.C. Mehendale

w: A hillside shrine to a four-peaked goddess - Chattushringi means 'four horns' - said to date to Shivaji's reign, reached by more than 200 steps up Senapati Bapat Road. Durga and Ganesh temples share the grounds, alongside eight miniature Ashtavinayaka idols scattered across the hillocks.
s: A four-peaked goddess, 200 steps up the hillside
_facts: Hindu temple on a hill on Senapati Bapat Road, said to have been built during Shivaji's reign
90 feet high, 125 feet wide; over 200 steps lead to the shrine
Temple complex also includes shrines to Durga and Ganesh, plus eight miniature Ashtavinayaka idols

w: Marks the exact spot where the Maratha commander-in-chief Mahadji Shinde was cremated in 1794 - a Shiva temple he'd built himself already stood there, and a formal memorial hall was added in 1910. The complex was commissioned by his Gwalior-royal descendants and built by a Bombay architectural firm.
s: Where a Maratha commander-in-chief was cremated
_facts: Memorial at Wanawadi to Maratha military leader Mahadji Shinde, commander-in-chief 1760-1780, marking his 1794 cremation site
A Shiva temple built by Shinde himself preceded the memorial; a samadhi was added in 1910
Complex commissioned by Maharaja Madho Rao Scindia of Gwalior, built by the firm of Shapurjee N. Chandabhoy of Bombay

w: A theatre and exhibition hall raised in memory of Bal Gangadhar Tilak, the firebrand nationalist and social reformer who became one of the loudest voices for Indian independence. Murals by Gopal Deuskar wrap the auditorium walls, tracing the key scenes of his life in paint rather than plaques.
s: A theatre-memorial to Bal Gangadhar Tilak
_facts: Theatre auditorium and exhibition hall dedicated to nationalist Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Features murals by Gopal Deuskar depicting events from Tilak's life
